reconcile.note: Gill limits Jesus's woe to praise bought by compromise with bad men, excepting the good word of good men, leaving the wisdom tradition's esteem for a good name untouched.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Daniel G. Taylor catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Daniel G. Taylor, BibViz Project (Bible Contradictions Visualized), citing EvilBible.com (2013).

sides.snippet: A good name is more desirable than great riches
sides.verseText: A good name is more desirable than great riches, And loving favor is better than silver and gold.

sides.snippet: Woe, when men speak well of you!
sides.verseText: Woe, when men speak well of you! For their fathers did the same thing to the false prophets.
